walk.environment:
Build: read-only worktree /tmp/claude-0/rewalk2/tree at 9eb10528. git status was clean before and after, and no .pyc was written. Launcher: /tmp/claude-0/rewalk2/out/O/scripts/launch.py, a Python exec wrapper that drops HTTP(S)_PROXY/ALL_PROXY (both cases), OO_DB_PASSPHRASE and OO_DB_PLAINTEXT, chdirs into the tree, and runs `python -c "from src.api.main import main; main()"` with PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 and OO_AUTOSEED=0, as the row's walks did. OO_NO_SCHEDULER was NOT set, so boot engaged airplane mode itself: the server log says 'Booted in airplane mode (offline)'. No data folder was copied from the old walks; every folder was seeded FRESH from the tree, so there was no stale briefing_cache.json.

Instance A (dataA, port 9618): the row's own seeds, run from the tree with OO_DB_PASSPHRASE=walk-pass-2026 and OO_DB_PLAINTEXT unset. They are docs/audit/living-sources-clickthrough-2026-09-25/seed.py, then storage-budgets-clickthrough-2026-09-25/seed.py, byte-identical to the re-walk's copies. The first 16 bytes of open_omniscience.db and wiki.db are ciphertext (no 'SQLite format 3' header). A booted with neither variable set, and /api/system/lock-state read {state: locked}. It was unlocked through the real #pw/#btn-unlock form, after which the state read unlocked-encrypted.

Instance B (dataB, port 9718): an empty encrypted corpus (init_db with the passphrase) plus scheduler_settings.json {"mode": "markets"}. It booted locked, was unlocked through the form, and was stopped by PID after the walk. O15a: A was shut down through the top-bar power icon and its confirm, cp -a copied to dataCopy, and the copy started on 9718, locked. The copy was shut down through the power icon, then deleted after a path check. All three servers are gone and ports 9618/9718 are free.

Network: airplane mode throughout. /api/system/network read {online:false} right after each unlock and at every check. No POST /api/system/network appears in any server log. Every consent popup was opened, read, screenshotted and closed with Stay offline / Rester hors ligne.

Browser: Playwright Chromium /opt/pw-browsers/chromium, headless, args --disable-background-networking --disable-component-update --no-proxy-server, proxy variables unset. Each run used a fresh context, so the offline coach was on its first launches. Passes: en at 1440x950; fr/ar/zh through the top-bar #lang-switch (live switches); 375x800 en; coach placement also in ar at 1024 and ar at 375. This disk had only 8.4 GB free, so the Storage 'budgets can still take' line is in the caveat colour even at the 20 GB default. That is correct arithmetic.

Scratch, scripts, logs, raw JSON: /tmp/claude-0/rewalk2/out/O/. Screenshots: /tmp/claude-0/rewalk2/out/O/shots/ (143 files).

Row O fails on one item: O-5 is still present on /tasks. Every walkable step passes.

The walk ran on build 9eb10528 with fresh encrypted folders, locked at boot and unlocked through the real form, in airplane mode throughout, in en, fr, ar and zh, at 1440, 1024 and 375 px. No page errors; nothing went online.

Steps: O1–O10 and O12 pass, and so do the encrypted-throwaway analogs O13a, O14a and O15a. O11's online half and O13–O15 on the maintainer's real install are not measurable here; O11's offline half was measured.

Items: five of six are fixed.
- O-1: the offline coach is now a strip inside the chrome. It covers 0 sampled points of the Living sources caveat, heading or Storage lines in every locale and width tried, and its arrow sits under the plane.
- O-2: the Preview targets line is translated in fr, ar and zh after a live switch, on a fresh load and after pressing.
- O-3: open stream and law diffs survive live language switches.
- O-4: French says 'voie' on every row-O surface; fr.json uses it on 36 of 36 lane keys and the glossary check reports 0 violations.
- O-6: clicking a tracked page no longer collapses an open diff.

O-5 is still present, on one of its three surfaces. Storage and Living sources → Maps are fixed in zh. The standalone task manager (/tasks) still prints '失败： HTTP 503 from the mirror' with an ASCII space after '：', because src/static/taskmanager.html:419 keeps its own `t(\"Failed:\") + \" \" + j.error` weld; only app-core.js's copy was changed.

Three incidental findings, none re-checked:

items.evidence:
I reproduced this on my own instance: a fresh data folder seeded from the tree with the row's two seeds (living-sources-clickthrough-2026-09-25/seed.py, then storage-budgets-clickthrough-2026-09-25/seed.py), OO_DB_PASSPHRASE=walk-pass-2026 set and OO_DB_PLAINTEXT unset. Neither database file starts with 'SQLite format 3'. The server booted on port 9668 with neither variable set. /api/system/lock-state read 'locked'; after unlocking through the real #pw/#btn-unlock form it read 'unlocked-encrypted'. The server log says 'Booted in airplane mode (offline)', and /api/system/network read {online:false} after unlock and again at the end. The log has no POST /api/system/network. I switched to 中文 with the top-bar #lang-switch, without reloading.

Two surfaces are fixed. Storage #storage-reading reads '本机（启动时读取）：4 个 CPU 核心 · …', and #storage-disk reads '…该驱动器有 8.1 GB 可用。这超过了该驱动器的可用空间。'. Living sources → Maps reads '失败：HTTP 503 from the mirror'. The regex [：。，；！？、）] followed by a space finds nothing on these surfaces, in innerText or in the stripped innerHTML.

The /tasks page is NOT fixed. I opened it three ways: from #tm-open after the live switch, from #tm-open after a full reload in zh, and by loading /tasks directly in a new page. Every time the page had <html lang=zh> and the #jobs-body failed row read '失败： HTTP 503 from the mirror'. The first code points of the line are U+5931 U+8D25 U+FF1A U+0020 U+0048: an ASCII space right after the full-width colon. The regex hits '： ' in both innerText and the stripped innerHTML. For contrast, en reads 'Failed: HTTP 503 from the mirror'. There were no page errors, no console errors and no HTTP responses >= 400. Screenshots: /tmp/claude-0/rewalk2/out/O-recheck/shots/O5-tasks-zh-live-crop.png (the gap is visible), O5-tasks-zh-live.png, O5-tasks-zh-reload.png, O5-storage-zh.png, O5-maps-zh.png. Raw data: /tmp/claude-0/rewalk2/out/O-recheck/raw-o5.json; script: /tmp/claude-0/rewalk2/out/O-recheck/scripts/o5.py. This is not a harness artifact: my script only reads the DOM, and the text comes straight from the page's own code.
items.root_cause: src/static/taskmanager.html:419. The standalone task-manager page (the page #tm-open opens; it is served by src/api/main.py:2845 and loads only i18n.js, not app-core.js) keeps its own copy of the failed-download line: jobWhy() does `line = t("Failed:") + " " + j.error;`. zh.json:2254 maps "Failed:" to "失败：", so the page prints full-width colon + ASCII space. The B-batch fix changed only the in-app copy, app-core.js:2154 (_jobWhy → ooLabelText(t("Failed"), j.error)). That copy uses the keyed frame "{prefix}: {text}", whose zh value is "{prefix}：{text}" (zh.json:4738). The standalone page's twin at taskmanager.html:419 was not updated. The comment at taskmanager.html:407-410 says the two are meant to stay in step.
items.suggested_fix: In src/static/taskmanager.html:419, replace the weld with the same keyed frame the in-app window uses. The page already has tf() (taskmanager.html:261) and t() (line 195): `line = tf("{prefix}: {text}", { prefix: t("Failed"), text: j.error });`. Both keys exist in all locales: "Failed" at zh.json:4557 and "{prefix}: {text}" at zh.json:4738. The result reads '失败：HTTP 503…' in zh, 'Échec : …' in fr and 'Failed: …' in en. Then grep taskmanager.html for any other `t("…:") + " "` welds.

recheck.summary: I confirmed O-5 on build 9eb10528 with my own encrypted instance (fresh seeds, port 9668, airplane mode throughout, unlocked through the real form). In 中文, Storage and Living sources → Maps no longer have a Latin space after full-width punctuation. The /tasks page, opened from #tm-open, still reads '失败： HTTP 503 from the mirror' (U+FF1A then U+0020) after a live switch, after a reload and on a direct load. The cause is src/static/taskmanager.html:419, which still does t("Failed:") + " " + j.error; only the in-app copy (app-core.js:2154) moved to ooLabelText. The fix is to use tf("{prefix}: {text}", {prefix: t("Failed"), text: j.error}) there. I saw nothing else broken while doing this. My server was stopped by PID 5605 and port 9668 is free. The worktree was not changed and no .pyc was written. Everything I wrote is under /tmp/claude-0/rewalk2/out/O-recheck/.
